title: Deterministic and stochastic operations
objectives: Build a matrix from its response to definite inputs.
Derive the distribution update p′=Mp and prove normalization preservation.
Distinguish stochastic validity, invertibility, and allowed reversal.

quizzes.question: In our column-vector convention, what does column j of an operation matrix describe?
options: The output distribution conditional on input j.
The input distribution conditional on output j.
The final distribution for every possible preparation.
feedback: Correct. Each input basis vector selects its corresponding output column.
That reverses the conditional direction. The input is the column label.
A different uncertain preparation combines the columns with different weights.

quizzes.question: Reset-to-zero preserves total probability. Must it therefore be reversible for every input?
options: Yes: preservation of probability guarantees an inverse.
No: distinct inputs are mapped to the same output.
Only if the input distribution is uniform.
feedback: Probability preservation is weaker than reversibility. Reset is a counterexample.
Correct. The common output cannot identify which of the distinct inputs occurred.
A chosen input distribution does not create an inverse that recovers every input.

source: Lecture Slides - 1 to 7.pdf, PDF pp.7,11. The total-probability derivation, random-flip calculation and distinction between algebraic and stochastic inverses expand the slide material.
prerequisites: Basic arithmetic and elementary algebra. A matrix-multiplication refresher is included before composition.
